name: Grid-forming inverters and synchronous condensers
principle: Grid-forming inverters set their own voltage and frequency, partly mimicking synchronous generators, whereas grid-following inverters need a stable grid to follow. Synchronous condensers add real inertia and short-circuit strength.

process_steps.name: Inverter sets voltage and frequency reference
Supply inertia-like response and fault current within limits

performance.metric: grid-following loss in Blue Cut Fire event, 2016
performance.basis: inverters tripped on faults under 60 ms

source.note: Wikipedia, Grid-forming inverter, read 25 October 2026 (secondary source)

performance.unit: MW discharge (100 MW / 129 MWh at Nov 2017 commissioning; expanded by 50 MW / 64.5 MWh from 2020)
performance.basis: world's first big battery, first 100 MW / 129 MWh completed November 2017 (hornsdalepowerreserve.com.au); AEMO approved Hornsdale's grid-forming inverters to deliver inertia services into the South Australian grid (Neoen)

source.note: Hornsdale Power Reserve official site; Neoen inertia-services announcement (read 2026-10-28)

limitations: Inverters tolerate only about 1 to 2 times rated current briefly versus 5 to 6 times for synchronous machines
